cmd00.name: PC-1 'Pathfinder' Probe Core
cmd00.summary: Minimal avionics puck for small satellites and landers.
cmd00.in_game: 0.08 t. 5 W idle. Hosts 2 internal slots (battery/computer). Basic SAS (stability only). Needs comms link for control beyond 2 km of a crewed vessel.
cmd00.real_life: CubeSat/SmallSat bus avionics (e.g. Blue Canyon XACT-class).

cmd01.name: PC-2 'Surveyor' Probe Bus
cmd01.summary: Hexagonal probe bus with internal bays for science, batteries and reaction wheels.
cmd01.in_game: 0.35 t. 4 internal slots, 15 W idle. Full SAS incl. prograde/target hold. Integrated 50 Nm reaction wheel.

cmd02.name: PC-3 'Voyager' Deep Space Bus
cmd02.summary: Large probe bus with RTG mounting points, heavy thermal control and long-life avionics.
cmd02.in_game: 1.1 t. 8 internal slots. Radiation-hardened: no avionics faults beyond Jupiter. Autonomy level 3 (executes stored manoeuvre plans without link).

cmd03.name: CM-1 'Gemini' Two-Seat Capsule
cmd03.summary: Cramped two-seat capsule for short LEO missions and early career.
cmd03.in_game: 2.3 t (approx). Crew 2. 3 internal slots. Life support 2 crew-days built in. Ablative shield rated for LEO re-entry only (~8 km/s).

cmd04.name: CM-2 'Soyuz' Three-Seat Descent Module
cmd04.summary: Bell-shaped descent module; pairs with an orbital module and service module.
cmd04.in_game: 2.9 t. Crew 3. 4 internal slots. Semi-ballistic re-entry with lift offset. Soft-landing retro-rockets fire at 1 m above ground.

cmd05.name: CM-3 'Dragon' Crew Capsule
cmd05.summary: Four-seat capsule with side-mounted abort engines and a nose-cone-covered docking port.
cmd05.in_game: 7.5 t dry (approx). Crew 4 (up to 7 in LEO config). 6 slots. Integrated abort engines (8x ~70 kN, hypergolic). Docking port under hinged nosecone.

cmd06.name: CM-4 'Orion' Deep Space Capsule
cmd06.summary: Deep-space capsule with heavier shield for lunar-return velocities.
cmd06.in_game: 9.3 t (approx). Crew 4. 8 slots, 21-day crew consumables. Shield rated to ~11 km/s re-entry. Requires a service module for power beyond 6 h.
cmd06.real_life: NASA Orion MPCV (with ESA European Service Module).

cmd07.name: CM-5 'MAV' Ascent Cabin
cmd07.summary: Minimal pressurised cockpit for a Mars Ascent Vehicle. No heat shield: it is never meant to re-enter.
cmd07.in_game: 2.0 t. Crew 6 seated tight. 2 slots. 2 crew-days life support only. Cannot survive re-entry; must dock to orbiting ship.
cmd07.real_life: MAV from The Martian; NASA Mars Ascent Vehicle concepts.

cmd08.name: CM-6 'Hermes' Flight Deck
cmd08.summary: Command deck for large interplanetary ships: bridge, flight computers, crew stations.
cmd08.in_game: 4.8 t. Crew 2 at stations (other crew live in hab). 10 slots. Required to control ships over 200 t. Must be on the despun (non-rotating) core.
cmd08.real_life: Hermes bridge (The Martian); ISS US Lab-style command functions.

cmd09.name: CM-7 'Lander' Crew Cabin
cmd09.summary: Lightweight pressurised cabin with forward windows for landing, top docking hatch.
cmd09.in_game: 2.4 t. Crew 2. 4 slots. 3 crew-days consumables. Excellent downward visibility (landing camera bonus). No heat shield.
cmd09.real_life: Apollo LM ascent stage; Artemis HLS cabin concepts.

cmd10.name: SM-1 Service Module Bay
cmd10.summary: Unpressurised cylinder that houses the capsule's batteries, fuel cells, tanks and radiators.
cmd10.in_game: 0.6-2.0 t by size. 6-12 internal slots. Surface radiator panels built into skin. Separates before re-entry.
cmd10.real_life: Apollo SM; Orion ESM; Dragon trunk.

prop00.name: RCS-Q 'Quad' Thruster Block
prop00.summary: Four-nozzle monopropellant attitude thruster block, surface mounted.
prop00.in_game: 0.05 t. 4 x ~0.45 kN. Isp ~220 s vac. Draws hydrazine from internal tanks via plumbing. Needs line-of-sight feed to a monoprop tank.
prop00.real_life: Apollo/Shuttle RCS quads; Aerojet MR-106 class.

prop01.name: RCS-B Bipropellant RCS
prop01.summary: Higher-thrust hypergolic RCS for large ships and dockings.
prop01.in_game: 0.08 t. 4 x ~0.4 kN MMH/NTO, Isp ~290 s vac. Pulse-capable, unlimited restarts.

prop02.name: HT-1 'Hall' Hall-Effect Thruster
prop02.summary: Small electric thruster for satellites and station-keeping.
prop02.in_game: 0.03 t. ~0.08 N. Isp ~1,800 s. 1.5 kW. Xenon or krypton. Thrust too low to leave surface; works under time-warp.

prop03.name: IT-1 'NEXT' Gridded Ion Engine
prop03.summary: Efficient gridded ion engine for deep-space probes and tugs.
prop03.in_game: 0.06 t. ~0.24 N. Isp ~4,000 s. 7 kW. Xenon. Cluster up to 8 on a thruster plate.

prop04.name: IT-2 'Hermes' Heavy Ion Cluster
prop04.summary: Large ion/Hall engine cluster for crewed interplanetary ships.
prop04.in_game: 1.2 t. ~5 N total (approx). Isp ~3,500 s. 200 kW; requires reactor-class power. Continuous burn for weeks (time-warp safe).
prop04.real_life: Hermes (The Martian); NASA X3 nested Hall thruster / AEPS.

prop05.name: SRB-S 'Castor' Small Solid
prop05.summary: Strap-on solid booster for small launchers.
prop05.in_game: 7 t wet. ~500 kN, Isp ~265 s SL. Not throttleable, cannot shut down. Thrust curve set in VAB (throttle profile).

prop06.name: SRB-L 'Atlas' Large Solid
prop06.in_game: ~250 t wet (approx). ~6,000 kN SL, Isp ~245 s. Burn ~120 s. Must be decoupled radially.

prop07.name: LE-1 'Kestrel' Pressure-Fed Hypergolic
prop07.in_game: 0.1 t. ~40 kN vac. Isp ~320 s vac. Unlimited restarts, throttle 40-100%. MMH/NTO.
prop07.real_life: AJ10 (Apollo SPS / Delta II upper stage).

prop08.name: LE-2 'Merlin' Gas-Generator Kerolox
prop08.in_game: 0.47 t. ~850 kN SL / 930 kN vac. Isp ~282 s SL / 311 s vac. Throttle 40-100%. 3 restarts (TEA-TEB ignition).

prop09.name: LE-3 'Merlin-V' Vacuum Kerolox
prop09.in_game: 0.55 t. ~980 kN vac. Isp ~348 s vac. Cannot be fired at sea level (flow separation damage).

prop10.name: LE-4 'Raptor' Full-Flow Methalox
prop10.in_game: 1.6 t. ~2,300 kN SL. Isp ~330 s SL / 350 s vac. Throttle 40-100%. Methane allows Mars ISRU refuelling.

prop11.name: LE-5 'Raptor-V' Vacuum Methalox
prop11.in_game: 1.9 t. ~2,500 kN vac. Isp ~375 s vac. Needs gimballed sea-level engine for control; limited gimbal (2 deg).

prop12.name: LE-6 'RS-25' Staged-Combustion Hydrolox
prop12.summary: High-efficiency main engine for core stages.
prop12.in_game: 3.2 t. ~1,860 kN SL / 2,280 kN vac. Isp ~366 s SL / 452 s vac. Limited restarts (ground start only).

prop13.name: LE-7 'RL10' Expander Hydrolox
prop13.in_game: 0.3 t. ~110 kN vac. Isp ~460 s vac. 15 restarts. Hydrogen boil-off makes it poor for long missions without cryocoolers.

prop14.name: LE-8 'MAV' Methalox Ascent Engine
prop14.summary: Mid-size methalox engine for landers and ascent vehicles, fed by ISRU-made propellant.
prop14.in_game: 0.35 t. ~100 kN vac, Isp ~355 s vac / ~320 s at Mars surface. Deep throttle 20-100%.
prop14.real_life: MAV (The Martian); Blue Origin BE-7 / NASA methalox lander engines.

tank00.name: T-K1/K2/K3 LOX/RP-1 Tanks
tank00.summary: Common-bulkhead kerosene/oxygen tanks. Denser than methalox, storable fuel side.
tank00.in_game: Wet 4 / 32 / 110 t (approx), dry mass ~6%. Mixture ratio 2.3:1 O:F. LOX boil-off ~0.1%/day without insulation.
tank00.real_life: Falcon 9 stage tanks; Saturn V S-IC.

tank01.name: T-M1/M2/M3 Methalox Tanks
tank01.summary: Stainless or aluminium-lithium tanks for methane/oxygen. Refuelable in orbit and at Mars.
tank01.in_game: Wet 30 / 100 / 400 t (approx), dry ~7%. Ratio 3.6:1. Mild cryogenic boil-off (~0.05%/day) unless cryocooler fitted.

tank02.name: T-H1/H2/H3 Hydrolox Tanks
tank02.summary: Large, low-density tanks for liquid hydrogen and oxygen with spray-on foam insulation.
tank02.in_game: Wet 20 / 70 / 300 t (approx), dry ~10% (hydrogen is bulky). Ratio 6:1. LH2 boil-off ~1%/day unless cryocooler (needs 2 kW).
tank02.real_life: SLS core stage; Centaur; Shuttle External Tank.

tank03.name: T-HG1/HG2 Hypergolic Tanks
tank03.summary: Spherical titanium tanks for MMH and NTO. Long-term storable.
tank03.in_game: Wet 0.5 / 2.5 t. Zero boil-off. Toxic: crew EVA near leak causes hazard event. Ratio ~1.65:1.
tank03.real_life: Apollo SPS tanks; Dragon SuperDraco tanks.

tank04.name: T-XE1/XE2/XE3 Xenon COPV
tank04.summary: Carbon-overwrapped pressure vessels for xenon or krypton propellant.
tank04.in_game: Hold 0.1 / 0.5 / 4 t Xe. Dry ~12% of contents. Krypton option: cheaper, 30% less thrust per kW.

tank05.name: T-MP1/MP2 Monoprop (Hydrazine) Tanks
tank05.summary: Diaphragm tanks for RCS and small monoprop thrusters.
tank05.in_game: Hold 0.05 / 0.4 t. Must be internal or inside a service bay when flying in space for >30 days (freezing risk without heaters: 5 W).
tank05.real_life: Diaphragm hydrazine tanks on most satellites.

tank06.name: T-SOLID Propellant Loadout
tank06.summary: Solid motors are self-contained; propellant load chosen in the builder.
tank06.in_game: Set 50-100% fill; reduces thrust duration, not peak thrust. Ballast for tuning.
tank06.real_life: Real SRBs are cast to spec.

tank07.name: T-DP Drop Tanks
tank07.summary: Jettisonable external tanks for landers and boosters.
tank07.in_game: Fed to core via crossfeed line. 4% dry mass. Must be decoupled with radial decoupler.
tank07.real_life: Shuttle External Tank; Falcon Heavy crossfeed concept.

tank08.name: T-CRYO Cryocooler Upgrade
tank08.summary: Internal-slot active cooler that eliminates cryogenic boil-off.
tank08.in_game: 0.15 t. 1-3 kW depending on tank size. Adds heat load to thermal budget.

tank09.name: T-ISRU Surface Storage Tank
tank09.summary: Ground tank for storing ISRU-produced propellant at a base.
tank09.in_game: Holds 50 t methalox. Can transfer to landed vessels by hose within 30 m.
tank09.real_life: Mars Direct / NASA DRA 5.0 ISRU storage.

tank10.name: T-H2O Water / Consumables Tank
tank10.summary: Internal tank for water, which doubles as radiation shielding.
tank10.in_game: Holds 1 / 8 t water. Placed in hab walls gives -20% crew radiation dose.
tank10.real_life: ISS water tanks; water-wall shielding concepts.

station00.name: HM-1 'Destiny' Hab Module
station00.summary: Rigid aluminium pressurised module for living and working.
station00.in_game: 14 t. Crew capacity 3. 12 internal slots. Volume ~100 m3. Requires life support from module or linked module.

station01.name: HM-2 'BEAM' Expandable Module
station01.summary: Inflatable softgoods module; launches compact, expands on orbit.
station01.in_game: 1.4 t. Deploy takes 1 in-game day. 16 m3. Crew 1. Great mass-to-volume, weaker micrometeoroid resistance.

station02.name: HM-3 'B330' Large Inflatable
station02.summary: Large inflatable habitat for stations and transit.
station02.in_game: 20 t. 330 m3. Crew 6. 16 slots. Needs a rigid core node at each end.
station02.real_life: Bigelow B330; Sierra Space LIFE habitat.

station03.name: NM-1 Node (6-port)
station03.summary: Pressurised connector with six berthing/docking ports.
station03.in_game: 11 t. 6 ports. 4 slots. Routes power, data and air between all connected modules.

station04.name: AL-1 EVA Airlock
station04.summary: Crew and equipment airlock with suit storage.
station04.in_game: 6 t. Holds 2 suits. EVA prep time 2 h (skippable with 'airlock expertise'). Loses ~0.5 kg air per cycle.

station05.name: DP-S/DP-M Docking Ports
station05.summary: Androgynous docking ports for crew transfer.
station05.in_game: 0.1 / 0.3 t. Standard size must match (S: 0.8 m hatch, M: 1.2 m). Soft-capture then hard-dock sequence.

station06.name: CBM Berthing Ring
station06.summary: Large berthing ring used with the robotic arm; wider hatch for cargo racks.
station06.in_game: 0.5 t. Requires arm-assisted berthing (no active docking). Allows internal rack transfer.

station07.name: TR-1 Integrated Truss
station07.summary: Unpressurised structural truss for solar arrays, radiators, reactors.
station07.in_game: 2 t per 10 m. 4 internal service bays per segment. Carries power/data lines.

station08.name: RA-1 Robotic Arm
station08.summary: Station arm for berthing, EVA support and module relocation.
station08.in_game: 1.8 t. 7 joints. 1 kW. Can 'walk' between grapple fixtures.

station09.name: GR-HUB Spin Hub & Bearing
station09.summary: Rotary joint between the despun core and a spinning ring, with slip rings for power and data.
station09.in_game: 6 t. Max ring mass 300 t. Spin-up rate 0.1 rpm/min using integrated motors. Transfers power/data/air across the joint.
station09.real_life: Nautilus-X concept; ISS SARJ (solar alpha rotary joint) as a scaled analogue.

station10.name: GR-SPK Spoke / Elevator Tube
station10.summary: Pressurised spoke with ladder or elevator linking hub to ring.
station10.in_game: 1.2 t per 10 m. Crew transit time 30 s per 10 m. Gravity rises along its length.

station11.name: GR-SEG Ring Segment
station11.summary: Curved hab segment. Six to twelve form a ring.
station11.in_game: 8 t each. Crew 2 each. 8 slots. Ring radius set in builder (20-100 m); segment count auto-scales.
station11.real_life: Hermes ring (The Martian); Nautilus-X; Stanford torus (scaled down).

station12.name: GR-CR Counter-Rotating Ring
station12.summary: Second, counter-spinning ring that cancels net angular momentum.
station12.in_game: Same as ring segments. When paired, ship can attitude-manoeuvre while spun without gyroscopic resistance.
station12.real_life: Counter-rotating ring concepts (Nautilus-X, O'Neill cylinder pairs).

station13.name: GR-DS Despun Core Section
station13.summary: Non-rotating axial module where docking, the bridge and engines attach.
station13.in_game: 10 t. 3 docking ports. Required: docking to a spinning module is impossible.

power00.name: SA-S Roll-Out Solar Array
power00.summary: Compact flexible roll-out wing for probes.
power00.in_game: 0.05 t. ~1.5 kW at 1 AU (scales 1/d^2). Single-axis tracking.

power01.name: SA-L Large Solar Wing
power01.in_game: 1.1 t. ~30 kW at 1 AU. Must be retracted before burns >0.2 g or it breaks.

power02.name: SA-X Ion-Tug Solar Array
power02.summary: Huge array for solar-electric propulsion ships.
power02.in_game: 3 t. ~100 kW at 1 AU; ~43 kW at Mars.
power02.real_life: Hermes arrays (The Martian); NASA Gateway PPE.

power03.name: RTG-1 MMRTG
power03.summary: Plutonium-238 radioisotope generator, needs no sunlight.
power03.in_game: 0.045 t. ~110 W electric, ~2 kW waste heat. Decays ~1.6%/yr. Must be mounted outside (heat). Radiation hazard during EVA within 3 m.

power04.name: FC-1 Fuel Cell Stack
power04.summary: Hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell, makes power and drinking water.
power04.in_game: 0.12 t. 5 kW. Consumes ~0.4 kg H2+O2 per kWh; outputs water to life support.

power05.name: BAT-S/M/L Internal Battery Packs
power05.summary: Lithium-ion packs installed only in internal slots.
power05.in_game: 0.05 / 0.2 / 1 t. 5 / 25 / 120 kWh. Heat 3% of throughput. Will not attach to exterior surfaces.

power06.name: FR-1 'Kilopower' Fission Reactor
power06.summary: Compact fission reactor with Stirling converters.
power06.in_game: 1.5 t. 10 kWe (40 kW upgrade variant: 4 t). Needs radiator. Shadow shield: crew must be in cone behind it.
power06.real_life: NASA KRUSTY / Kilopower; Fission Surface Power.

power07.name: FR-2 Megawatt-Class Reactor
power07.summary: Large reactor for heavy ion ships (the one 'stretch' item).
power07.in_game: 12 t. ~1 MWe (approx). Needs radiator area ~600 m2. Scram if coolant lost.
power07.real_life: NASA SP-100 / Prometheus concepts; Hermes reactor (The Martian).

power08.name: RAD-S/L Radiator Panels
power08.summary: Deployable heat-rejection panels with ammonia loops.
power08.in_game: 0.1 / 1.5 t. Reject 3 / 70 kW. Must face away from the Sun for full rating.

power09.name: LT-1 Floodlight
power09.summary: Exterior LED floodlight for docking and night landings.
power09.in_game: 0.01 t. 50 W. Illuminates 60 deg cone, 40 m range.

power11.name: COM-2 High-Gain Dish
power11.summary: Steerable parabolic dish for interplanetary data.
power11.in_game: 0.15 t. 100 W. Range to outer planets. Must point at relay or ground station.
power11.real_life: Juno / MRO high-gain antenna; DSN link.

power12.name: LS-1 Life Support Rack
power12.summary: Oxygen generation, CO2 scrubbing and water recovery.
power12.in_game: 0.6 t. 1.5 kW. Supports 3 crew. Recovers ~93% of water; O2 from electrolysis.

power13.name: LS-2 Consumables Pallet
power13.in_game: 0.3 t per 30 crew-days (approx 1.8 kg food/crew/day with packaging).
power13.real_life: ISS cargo bags; Hab supplies (The Martian).

stage00.name: DC-S/M/L/XL Stack Decoupler
stage00.in_game: 0.05-0.8 t by size. Ejection force set 0-200 kN. Leaves ring on lower stage.
stage00.real_life: Falcon 9 pneumatic stage separation; Saturn interstage rings.

stage01.name: DC-R Radial Decoupler
stage01.summary: Side-mount decoupler for boosters and drop tanks.
stage01.in_game: 0.05 t. Kicks boosters outward. Includes separation motors.

stage02.name: SP-HOT Hot-Staging Ring
stage02.summary: Vented interstage allowing upper stage ignition before separation.
stage02.in_game: 0.3-1.2 t. Removes ullage loss. Must be jettisoned after staging.

stage03.name: IS-1 Interstage Adapter
stage03.summary: Conical/cylindrical adapters between diameters (S-M, M-L, L-XL, XL-XXL).
stage03.in_game: Mass ~2% of the stage above. Can enclose an engine bell.

stage04.name: FR-S/M/L/XL Payload Fairing
stage04.summary: Clamshell fairing built around payload in the builder.
stage04.in_game: Mass by area (~20 kg/m2). Shields payload from drag and heating. Jettison above ~100 km.

stage05.name: HS-S/M/L/XL Ablative Heat Shield
stage05.in_game: Ablator mass tracked; 1 kg burns per ~0.5 MJ. Rated velocity by variant (LEO / Lunar return).

stage06.name: HIAD Inflatable Decelerator
stage06.summary: Inflatable heat shield for landing heavy payloads on Mars.
stage06.in_game: 1.5 t. Deploys to 3x diameter. Single use.

stage07.name: PC-D Drogue Parachute
stage07.in_game: Safe to deploy below Mach 1.5. Reduces tumbling.

stage08.name: PC-M Main Parachute
stage08.in_game: One chute slows 3 t to ~9 m/s on Earth. Mars air 1% of Earth: chute alone is not enough.

stage09.name: PC-SS Supersonic Mars Chute
stage09.in_game: Deploys Mach 2. Reduces velocity to ~80 m/s; must be followed by retro-propulsion.

stage10.name: GF-1 Titanium Grid Fins
stage10.summary: Lattice fins for steering returning boosters.
stage10.in_game: 0.1 / 0.4 t. Effective Mach 0.5-4. Stowed during ascent.

stage11.name: LL-S/M/L Landing Legs
stage11.in_game: Rated touchdown ~3 / 5 / 6 m/s. Max slope 12 deg.

rover00.name: RV-1 'Sojourner' Micro Rover
rover00.in_game: 0.01 t. 0.01 m/s. Runs from solar and internal battery.

rover01.name: RV-2 'Curiosity' Science Rover
rover01.in_game: 0.9 t. MMRTG power. 0.04 m/s. 6 internal science slots, robotic arm.

rover02.name: RV-3 'LRV' Open Rover
rover02.summary: Unpressurised two-seat rover; crew in suits.
rover02.in_game: 0.21 t. Top speed ~3 m/s. ~9 kWh internal battery. Suit oxygen limits range to ~10 km from base.

rover03.name: RV-4 Pressurised Rover
rover03.summary: Long-range pressurised rover with airlock and sleep space.
rover03.in_game: 7 t. Crew 2 (4 tight). Life support 14 days. 8 slots. Top speed 5 m/s.
rover03.real_life: Martian rover (The Martian); NASA SEV / Toyota Lunar Cruiser.

rover04.name: WH-S/M/L Wheels
rover04.in_game: Load 50 / 500 / 3,000 kg per wheel in 1 g equivalent. Slip on regolith modelled.
rover04.real_life: Apollo mesh wheels; Curiosity aluminium wheels.

rover05.name: DR-1 Core Drill
rover05.in_game: 0.05 t. 400 W. Up to 2 m depth. Produces sample for science racks.

rover06.name: DR-2 Regolith Excavator
rover06.in_game: 0.3 t. 2 kW. 200 kg regolith / hour. Picks up water ice where present.

rover07.name: ISRU-O2 MOXIE Oxygen Plant
rover07.summary: Solid-oxide electrolysis of Mars CO2 into oxygen.
rover07.in_game: 0.2 t. 1.5 kW. ~1 kg O2/day for the scaled-up unit (the real demo unit made only grams per hour).

rover08.name: ISRU-S Sabatier Reactor
rover08.summary: Combines CO2 and hydrogen into methane and water.
rover08.in_game: 1.5 t. 25 kW. ~20 kg CH4/day (approx). Needs H2 feed or water electrolysis.
rover08.real_life: Sabatier reactor on ISS; MAV fuel plant (The Martian).

rover09.name: ISRU-W Water Extractor
rover09.in_game: 1 t. 15 kW. 30 kg water/day from 5% ice regolith.

rover10.name: SH-1 Surface Hab (Rigid)
rover10.real_life: NASA DRA habitat; Artemis surface habitat.

rover11.name: SH-2 'Hab' Inflatable Dome
rover11.summary: Inflatable dome habitat like The Martian's Hab.
rover11.in_game: 5 t packed. 90 m3 deployed. Crew 6. Needs airlock unit; puncture event if struck.
rover11.real_life: The Martian Hab; NASA inflatable surface habitats.

rover12.name: SH-3 Greenhouse Module
rover12.in_game: 3 t. 5 kW lighting. Produces food 0.5 kg/day + O2. Needs water.
rover12.real_life: NASA Veggie; Watney's potato farm (The Martian).

jet00.name: JT-1 Turbojet
jet00.in_game: 1.8 t. ~50 kN dry / 80 kN wet. Isp ~1,800 s dry. Mach 0-2.5. Needs air intake.

jet01.name: JT-2 High-Bypass Turbofan
jet01.summary: Efficient subsonic turbofan for cargo carriers.

jet02.name: JT-3 Low-Bypass Turbofan
jet02.in_game: 1.7 t. ~110 kN wet. Mach 0-2. Good thrust-to-weight.

jet03.name: JT-4 Turbo-Ramjet
jet03.summary: Combined cycle engine that becomes a ramjet at high Mach.
jet03.in_game: 3.0 t. ~150 kN. Effective Mach 0-3.2. Heat warning above 3.2.

jet04.name: RJ-1 Ramjet
jet04.summary: Pure ramjet: no thrust below Mach 0.8.
jet04.in_game: 0.5 t. ~60 kN at Mach 2.5. Effective Mach 1-4.

jet05.name: SJ-1 Experimental Scramjet
jet05.in_game: 0.6 t. ~40 kN, Mach 5-7 only. Overheats quickly. Marked 'experimental'.

jet07.name: IN-2 Shock-Cone Intake
jet07.summary: Translating spike intake for high Mach.

jet08.name: WG-1 Wing Panels (Straight / Swept / Delta)
jet08.in_game: Lift from area; delta handles re-entry heating best. Mass ~25 kg/m2.

jet09.name: CS-1 Control Surfaces (Elevon / Rudder / Canard)
jet09.summary: Movable surfaces for pitch, yaw, roll.
jet09.in_game: Deflect up to 25 deg. Ineffective above ~50 km altitude; use RCS.

jet10.name: LG-S/M/L Landing Gear
jet10.in_game: Rated for 5 / 30 / 150 t aircraft. Max touchdown 70-100 m/s.

jet11.name: TPS-T Thermal Tile Kit
jet11.summary: Silica tiles and reinforced carbon edges for spaceplanes.
jet11.in_game: Adds 12 kg/m2. Reusable. Individual tiles can be lost under stress.
jet11.real_life: Shuttle TPS tiles / RCC; Dream Chaser tiles.

cockpit00.name: CK-1 Single-Seat Jet Cockpit
cockpit00.summary: Single-seat jet nose with a one-piece bubble canopy, ejection seat and radome.
cockpit00.in_game: 0.9 t. Crew 1. 360 deg view; canopy opens on the ground only. Ejection seat usable below Mach 2 / 15 km. No re-entry rating.

cockpit01.name: CK-2 Tandem Two-Seat Cockpit
cockpit01.summary: Two-seat tandem nose, rear seat raised for forward view, twin clamshell canopies.
cockpit01.in_game: 1.4 t. Crew 2. Canopies open on the ground only. Rated to Mach 3.2 skin heating with a heat penalty above that.

cockpit02.name: CK-3 Spaceplane Flight Deck
cockpit02.summary: Side-by-side crewed nose for spaceplanes: flight deck windows, forward RCS, RCC nose cap and black belly tiles.
cockpit02.in_game: 3.2 t. Crew 2 (+2 mid-deck). Re-entry rated belly-first at 40 deg AoA. Includes 11 forward RCS jets on the shared RCS supply. Rear joins a Mk2-style fuselage.
cockpit02.real_life: Space Shuttle orbiter forward fuselage; Dream Chaser.

cockpit03.name: CK-4 Airliner / Cargo Flight Deck
cockpit03.summary: Airliner / cargo-lifter nose with a raised flight deck and an optional hinged cargo visor.
cockpit03.in_game: 4.5 t. Crew 3. Visor opens on the ground for straight-in loading of S/M cargo (1.95 m aperture). Subsonic only (Mach 0.9).
cockpit03.real_life: Boeing 747-400F nose door; Lockheed C-5 Galaxy visor.

cockpit04.name: CK-5 Inline Cockpit (Droop Nose)
cockpit04.summary: Mid-fuselage cockpit ring with side windows that sits behind a nose cone; includes a droop-nose hinge.
cockpit04.in_game: 2.1 t. Crew 3. Front S node takes a nose cone; droop 12.5 deg for take-off and landing view. Supersonic rated (Mach 2.2).
cockpit04.real_life: Concorde droop nose and visor; XB-70 Valkyrie.

cockpit05.name: CK-6 Uncrewed Avionics Nose
cockpit05.summary: Uncrewed probe core for drones and robotic spaceplanes: bulged satcom radome and chin sensor ball.
cockpit05.in_game: 0.35 t. No crew. Autopilot and SAS, long-range comms, EO/IR sensor ball for surveying. Needs power 0.4 kW.
cockpit05.real_life: RQ-4 Global Hawk nose; X-37B OTV.

rover13.name: CH-F Rover Chassis Frame
rover13.summary: Kit backbone with a 0.5 m node grid, suspension rail hardpoints and front/rear faces.
rover13.in_game: Backbone of every kit rover. Top and underside expose a 0.5 m grid of attach nodes; side rails carry suspension/steering hardpoints every 0.5 m; front and rear faces take bumpers, blades, hitches or another frame. Distributes power, data and coolant to everything on the grid. Mass 0.015 / 0.05 / 0.18 / 0.45 t; rated deck load 0.1 / 0.6 / 3 / 10 t (1 g).
rover13.real_life: Apollo Lunar Roving Vehicle aluminium chassis; NASA Chariot / Lunar Electric Rover chassis

rover14.name: CH-P Chassis Deck Plate
rover14.summary: Thin gridded plate to extend, bridge or outrigger chassis frames.
rover14.in_game: Extends or bridges chassis frames and makes outriggers. Same 0.5 m grid on both faces plus edge nodes, so plates tile edge to edge or bolt on top of a frame. 0.05 m thick, 12 kg/m2. Not a structural spine: max span load 0.5 t per plate.
rover14.real_life: LRV floor panels; aluminium honeycomb sandwich panels used on spacecraft decks

rover15.name: CH-J Articulated Chassis Joint
rover15.summary: Powered yaw / free roll joint linking two frames for articulated steering.
rover15.in_game: Joins two frames end to end (node_front / node_rear). Powered yaw +/-35 deg gives articulated steering without steerable wheels; free roll +/-15 deg keeps all wheels on the ground over rocks. Passes power, data and coolant. Mass 0.04 / 0.15 t; rated 2 / 10 t.
rover15.real_life: Articulated-frame steering (articulated haulers); Marsokhod / NASA Chariot articulated rovers

rover16.name: SU-RB Rocker-Bogie Suspension
rover16.summary: Passive six-wheel rocker-bogie side unit for slow, rock-climbing rovers.
rover16.in_game: One side of a six-wheel passive suspension (fit a mirrored pair joined by the frame's differential bar). Climbs obstacles up to one wheel diameter at walking pace; no springs, so top speed limited to ~0.2 m/s. Three node_outboard_N stations take steering modules, drive motors and rover04 wheels. Mass 0.004 / 0.03 / 0.12 t per side.

rover17.name: SU-A Independent Suspension Arm
rover17.summary: Sprung, damped double-wishbone arm for one wheel station.
rover17.in_game: Sprung, damped suspension for one wheel station. Bolts to a chassis rail node (node_attach) and carries a steering module or drive motor on node_outboard. Travel 0.1 / 0.2 / 0.3 m; spring rate auto-set from rover mass and local gravity; stiffness/damping sliders in the builder. Allows 1 / 3 / 5 m/s over rough ground. Mass 5 / 25 / 90 kg.
rover17.real_life: Apollo LRV torsion-bar double-wishbone suspension; Lunar Terrain Vehicle prototypes

rover18.name: ST-1 Steering Module
rover18.summary: Swivels a wheel station: Ackermann, crab or pivot-turn steering.
rover18.in_game: Swivels the wheel station about a vertical axis: +/-35 deg Ackermann, or +/-90 deg crab steer / pivot-turn mode for tight spaces and docking with habs. Sits between suspension (node_attach) and drive motor (node_outboard). 20 / 60 / 200 W while steering. Mass 3 / 10 / 35 kg.
rover18.real_life: Curiosity/Perseverance corner-wheel steering actuators; NASA SEV / Chariot crab steering

rover19.name: DM-1 Hub Drive Motor
rover19.summary: In-hub electric motor that drives one rover04 wheel.
rover19.in_game: Powers one wheel. Mounts on a steering module, suspension arm or directly on a rail; the matching rover04 wheel (S/M/L) fits node_outboard; XS is for micro rovers (needs a proposed 0.15 m rover04 XS wheel). Peak 0.005 / 0.1 / 0.5 / 2.5 kW, torque 1 / 30 / 250 / 1,500 Nm, top speed ~0.01 / 1 / 4 / 5 m/s with matching wheels. Waste heat 15% of draw; regen braking returns 10% downhill. Mass 0.3 / 4 / 15 / 60 kg.
rover19.real_life: Apollo LRV hub traction drive; Curiosity wheel drive actuators

rover20.name: TK-1 Track Unit
rover20.summary: Tracked unit for soft regolith and steep slopes; slower, power-hungry.
rover20.in_game: Replaces a wheel station on soft regolith, dunes and snow: ground pressure 1/4 of a wheel, climbs 30 deg slopes, but top speed 1.5 m/s and 2x drive power. Integrated drive motor; mounts on a rail node or suspension arm. 0.4 / 2.0 kW. Mass 45 / 220 kg.
rover20.real_life: Rubber track conversion units (e.g. Mattracks); tracked planetary rover prototypes

rover21.name: RC-1 Rover Control Core
rover21.summary: Rover probe core: drive computer, hazcams, autonav, 1 Small slot.
rover21.in_game: The probe core for rovers: drive computer, IMU, hazard cameras and autonomous navigation (drives waypoints without link). Includes a 1-unit Small internal slot (battery, computer or science). Provides traction control and wheel-slip limiting. Top node takes a mast or science turret. 60 W. Mass 25 kg. One per rover (or a crewed cab).
rover21.real_life: Curiosity / Perseverance rover compute element and hazcams

rover22.name: SE-1 Suited Crew Seat
rover22.summary: Open seat with hand controller for one suited crew member.
rover22.in_game: Open seat for one suited crew member; mounts on any grid node. Includes a hand controller, so a seat plus a control core (or open cab) makes a drivable rover. Crew breathe from suits: range limited by suit consumables. Folds flat for launch. Mass 12 kg.
rover22.real_life: Apollo LRV seats and T-handle hand controller

rover23.name: CB-O Open Cab Frame
rover23.summary: Open driving station: console, roll hoop and two seat nodes.
rover23.in_game: Driving station for suited crew: console with nav display and comms relay (links suits to the rover antenna), roll-over protection and two seat nodes (take rover22 seats). Console top node takes an antenna mast or camera. 40 W. Mass 55 kg.
rover23.real_life: Apollo LRV control and display console; Artemis Lunar Terrain Vehicle

rover24.name: CB-P Pressurised Rover Cab
rover24.summary: Shirt-sleeve cab with suitports and docking hatch (crew 2 or 4).
rover24.in_game: Shirt-sleeve cab for long traverses. Rear suitports give 10-minute EVA egress without an airlock; top-rear hatch docks to habs and ascent vehicles. M: crew 2, 10 m3, built-in life support for 2 crew x 3 days, 4 Small + 1 Medium slots. L: crew 4 (2 sleep), 22 m3, 8 Small + 2 Medium + 1 Rack slot (fit LS-1 for long trips). 0.4 / 0.8 kW idle. Mass 2.4 / 4.5 t.
rover24.real_life: NASA Space Exploration Vehicle; JAXA/Toyota Lunar Cruiser; The Martian rover

rover25.name: CG-1 Cargo Bed
rover25.summary: Gridded flatbed for surface cargo, with fold-down tailgate ramp.
rover25.in_game: Carries surface cargo: sample boxes, tanks, rolled-up solar arrays, spare wheels, a Sojourner-class micro rover. Floor has its own 0.5 m grid so containers snap in; tie-downs keep cargo attached at up to 3 m/s bumps. Tailgate folds into a ramp. Payload 0.3 / 1.5 t (1 g). Mass 30 / 90 kg.
rover25.real_life: Apollo LRV aft tool pallet; Apollo 14 Modular Equipment Transporter

rover26.name: BB-1 Rover Battery Bay
rover26.summary: Heated enclosure that gives the deck internal slots for batteries.
rover26.in_game: Thermally controlled enclosure that turns deck space into internal slots, so batteries stay internal per the build rules. S: 2 Small slots; M: 4 Small or 1 Medium. Takes power05 BAT packs, fuel cells or computers; heaters draw 10 / 20 W in the cold (0 W if warmed by an RTG mount). Lid top node takes a solar or radiator panel. Mass 15 / 35 kg empty.
rover26.real_life: Apollo LRV battery housings; Curiosity rover warm electronics box

rover27.name: RD-R Rover Radiator
rover27.summary: Deck radiator with a dust cover that opens at stops.
rover27.in_game: Rejects rover heat (drive motors, cab, electronics): 0.5 / 2 kW with the cover open and the panel out of direct sun. Cover closes while driving to keep dust off (dusty radiators lose 50%); opens automatically at stops. Mass 12 / 40 kg.
rover27.real_life: Apollo LRV radiators with dust covers (the Apollo 17 fender/dust incident)

rover28.name: SA-R Rover Solar Mount
rover28.summary: Fold-out, sun-tilting solar array for parked rovers.
rover28.in_game: Unfolds and tilts to track the Sun when parked (fixed flat while driving). 0.35 / 1.2 kW at 1 AU, ~43% at Mars, dust loss 0.2%/sol unless wiped by crew or wind. Folds for dust storms and transport. Mass 20 / 60 kg.
rover28.real_life: Mars Exploration Rover (Spirit/Opportunity) solar deck; VIPER solar panels

rover29.name: RM-1 RTG Mount
rover29.summary: Rear RTG cradle that pipes waste heat into the rover's thermal loop.
rover29.in_game: Holds a power03 MMRTG on the rear of the chassis at 30 deg so its fins shed heat. Heat exchangers pipe ~1.5 kW of RTG waste heat into the rover coolant loop: battery bays and cabs need no heater power. Shield plate lets crew work at the front of the rover. Mass 18 kg.
rover29.real_life: Curiosity / Perseverance MMRTG mount with heat exchangers

rover30.name: TA-1 Rover Robotic Arm
rover30.summary: 5-DoF arm with drill / contact-sensor / scoop tool turret.
rover30.in_game: 5-DoF arm with a three-position tool turret: core drill (rover05 head), contact sensor head (reads through sci01 in a core slot) and a sampling scoop. Places sci02 seismometers and moves cargo up to 5 / 20 kg. Reach 1.8 / 3.0 m. 150 / 400 W. Mass 70 / 160 kg.
rover30.real_life: Curiosity / Perseverance robotic arm and turret

rover31.name: TD-1 Drill Mast
rover31.summary: Fold-up drill derrick for 3 m deep sampling and ice prospecting.
rover31.in_game: Vertical feed mast for deep sampling and ice prospecting: carries the rover05 drill head down to 3 m using a 4-rod carousel (vs 2 m on the arm). Finds subsurface ice for ISRU siting. 300 W while drilling, 0.3 m/h in rock. Rover must be parked. Mass 60 kg.
rover31.real_life: ExoMars Rosalind Franklin drill; Honeybee TRIDENT drill (VIPER)

rover32.name: TS-1 Dozer Blade & Scoop
rover32.summary: Front blade that grades pads, builds berms and scoops regolith.
rover32.in_game: Grades landing pads, pushes regolith berms around reactors and habs (radiation and blast protection) and loads regolith into rover09/DR-2 feed hoppers. 0.1 / 0.3 / 0.8 m3 per pass. Needs traction: works best on heavy rovers or tracks. 0.2 / 0.6 / 1.5 kW. Mass 40 / 120 / 300 kg.
rover32.real_life: NASA Chariot / Lunar dozer-blade prototypes; Phoenix lander scoop

rover33.name: SC-T Science Turret
rover33.summary: Remote-sensing mast with built-in cameras and laser spectrometer.
rover33.in_game: Science is built in, not bolted on: the head integrates stereo panoramic cameras, a laser-induced breakdown spectrometer and an IR spectrometer, with electronics in the base's Small slot. Zaps rocks up to 7 m away for biome/rock science without stopping; also the rover's best navigation camera. 80 W. Mass 35 kg.
rover33.real_life: Curiosity Mastcam + ChemCam; Perseverance Mastcam-Z + SuperCam

rover34.name: BP-1 Bumper / Push Bar
rover34.summary: Crush-box bumper with tow eye; mounts front or rear.
rover34.in_game: Mounts on node_front or node_rear. Crush boxes absorb a 3 m/s collision without damaging the frame (single use per box; repairable by crew EVA). Tow eye lets one rover pull another out of a sand trap. Top rail takes light bars. Mass 10 / 25 / 50 kg.
rover34.real_life: Off-road vehicle bull bars; NASA Chariot rover bumpers

rover35.name: LB-1 Rover Light Bar
rover35.summary: LED spot/flood light bar for night and shadowed craters.
rover35.in_game: Driving lights for night and permanently shadowed craters: 30 deg spot beams to 60 m plus 90 deg flood to 20 m. 40 / 120 W. Mounts on the grid, cab roof, roll hoop or bumper top. Hazard cameras need it to drive in the dark. Mass 3 / 7 kg.
rover35.real_life: NASA VIPER rover headlights; off-road LED light bars

rover36.name: AM-1 Antenna Mast
rover36.summary: Telescoping mast with omni and small dish; extends link range.
rover36.in_game: Rover comms: omni plus a 0.6 m steerable dish. Extending the mast from 0.8 to 3 m pushes the radio horizon out (about 2x link range to nearby landers and base) and clears the crest of crater rims. Relays suit radios. 25 W. Mass 15 kg. Also mounts on the open-cab console.
rover36.real_life: Apollo LRV umbrella high-gain antenna; Curiosity high-gain antenna

rover37.name: HC-1 Hitch / Trailer Coupler
rover37.summary: Tow hitch with power/data umbilical (active and passive halves).
rover37.in_game: Couples a rover to a trailer or another rover. Active half on the tow vehicle, passive half on the trailer tongue; couples within 0.2 m and 20 deg. Passes power and data (and air on the pressurised variant) so a trailer's batteries, RTG or hab share the rover's bus. Pulls 10 t (1 g). Mass 8 kg.
rover37.real_life: Tow hitches with umbilicals; The Martian rover towing the Hab trailer

rover38.name: TF-1 Trailer Frame
rover38.summary: Unpowered towed chassis with the same grid and rail nodes.
rover38.in_game: Unpowered chassis towed via the hitch coupler. Same deck grid and rail hardpoints as rover13, so it takes suspension, wheels, cargo beds, battery bays, RTG mounts or even a rover10 hab. Unpowered wheels still need suspension arms. Mass 0.06 / 0.2 t; rated 1 / 5 t.
rover38.real_life: Apollo 14 Modular Equipment Transporter; Watney's rover trailer (The Martian)

rover39.name: ISRU-E Water Electrolyser
rover39.summary: Medium-slot electrolyser: water to hydrogen and oxygen.
rover39.in_game: Medium slot item (1.0 x 1.0 x 0.6 m). Splits water from rover09 extractors or tank10 into H2 and O2: 5 kW gives ~0.9 kg water/h -> 0.1 kg H2 + 0.8 kg O2. Feeds rover08 Sabatier (H2) and oxidiser tanks; with tank08 cryocoolers this closes the Mars/Moon methalox loop. Heat 1 kW. Mass 0.18 t.
rover39.real_life: PEM water electrolysers; ISS Oxygen Generation System electrolysis cell stack

prop15.name: LE-9 'Rutherford' Electric-Pump Kerolox
prop15.summary: Small kerolox engine with battery-driven electric pumps.
prop15.in_game: Small-launcher engine whose pumps are driven by electric motors: it draws ~50 kW from BAT packs in the stage's internal slots (~0.8 kWh per minute of burn), so the builder checks battery capacity against burn time. 25 kN SL / 26 kN vac; Isp ~300 s SL; vacuum-nozzle variant 26 kN, ~340 s. Throttle 50-100%, 3 restarts. Mass 0.035 t.

prop16.name: LE-10 'Spike' Methalox Aerospike
prop16.summary: Altitude-compensating methalox plug nozzle (toroidal or linear).
prop16.in_game: Altitude-compensating engine: nearly flat Isp from sea level to vacuum (~320 s SL / ~345 s vac), so one engine does the whole ascent. 850 kN SL. No gimbal; steers by differential throttling of chamber segments. Heavy (2.2 t) and the plug runs hot (heat load 2x a bell engine). Toroidal (round, stack) and linear (fits Mk2/Mk3 tails) variants.
prop16.real_life: Rocketdyne XRS-2200 linear aerospike (X-33); J-2T toroidal aerospike

prop17.name: VN-1 Vernier Thruster
prop17.summary: Small swivelling radial engine for roll control and trim.
prop17.in_game: Radial helper engine fed from the main tanks (kerolox or methalox). Swivels +/-45 deg on one axis for roll control and fine velocity trim after main-engine cutoff. 10 kN, Isp ~260 s SL / 300 s vac. Fit in pairs or fours. Mass 25 kg.
prop17.real_life: Atlas LR101 vernier; Soyuz / R-7 vernier thrusters

prop18.name: LE-11 'F-1' Heavy Gas-Generator Kerolox
prop18.summary: Huge single-chamber booster engine for super-heavy first stages.
prop18.in_game: Biggest single-chamber engine in the game for super-heavy first stages. 6,770 kN SL / 7,770 kN vac, Isp 263 s SL / 304 s vac. No throttle, no restart (single hypergolic ignition cartridge). Needs an L or larger thrust structure. Mass 8.4 t.

prop19.name: LE-12 'LMDE' Deep-Throttle Descent Engine
prop19.summary: Hypergolic lander engine with 10-100% deep throttle.
prop19.in_game: Lander descent engine with a 10-100% throttle (pintle injector), the best hover and landing control in the game. M: 45 kN vac, Isp 311 s, gimbal 6 deg; S: scaled 15 kN. Nozzle extension crushes on touchdown without damage (so landers can sit low). Mass 0.18 / 0.07 t.
prop19.real_life: TRW Lunar Module Descent Engine (Apollo LM)

prop20.name: AE-1 'LEROS' Apogee Engine
prop20.summary: Tiny radiatively cooled probe engine for orbit insertion burns.
prop20.in_game: Probe main engine for orbit insertion burns: 0.64 kN, Isp ~320 s vac, MMH/NTO from tank03. Unlimited restarts and hour-long burns; nozzle glows cherry red (needs a clear view of space to cool). Mass 5 kg.

prop21.name: SRB-M 'Castor-M' Medium Solid
prop21.summary: Mid-size solid, as a strap-on or a small launcher's core stage.
prop21.in_game: Fills the gap between SRB-S and SRB-L. ~55 t wet, 1,700 kN SL, Isp ~275 s SL / 290 s vac, burn ~90 s. Strap-on variant (nosecone, radial attach) or core variant (flat top, stack nodes, +/-5 deg thrust vectoring) for small launcher first stages. Cannot shut down.
prop21.real_life: Avio P120C / Vega P80; Northrop Grumman Castor 30

prop22.name: UM-1 Ullage / Retro Motor Pack
prop22.summary: Tiny solids that settle propellant before restarts or push stages away.
prop22.in_game: Small solids that fire for 2-4 s. Ullage variant (nozzles aft) settles propellant before an engine restart in free fall; engines flagged 'needs ullage' fail to relight without it or RCS thrust. Retro variant (nozzles canted forward) pushes a spent stage away after separation. 3 x 10 kN. Mass 45 kg.
prop22.real_life: Saturn V S-II ullage motors and S-IC retro-rockets

prop23.name: KS-1 'Star-48' Kick Motor
prop23.summary: Spherical solid upper-stage motor for probe escape burns.
prop23.in_game: Upper-stage solid for escape burns on small probes: 2.1 t, 68 kN vac, Isp 286 s, 85 s burn. Cannot throttle or stop, so the builder plans the burn in advance. Spin-table variant spins the stack to 60 rpm for stability (no guidance needed); 3-axis variant needs a probe core.

prop24.name: LES-1 Launch Escape Tower
prop24.summary: Tractor abort tower that pulls a capsule clear, then jettisons.
prop24.in_game: Tractor abort system for capsules without built-in abort engines (cmd03/04/06). On abort it pulls the capsule 1+ km clear in 3-4 s (M 700 kN / L 1,000 kN / XL 1,800 kN), canards flip it heat-shield first, then it jettisons. Jettisoned normally ~3 min after launch. Mass 2.5 / 4.2 / 7.3 t.
prop24.real_life: Apollo Launch Escape System; Orion Launch Abort System

prop25.name: CG-1 Cold-Gas Thruster Block
prop25.summary: Non-toxic nitrogen RCS, safe near crew and solar arrays.
prop25.in_game: Simplest RCS: nitrogen gas from a tank04 COPV (N2 fill). 4 x 20 N, Isp ~65 s. Non-toxic and cold, so it is safe near crew on EVA and around station solar arrays (no plume contamination). Mass 3 kg.
prop25.real_life: Manned Maneuvering Unit nitrogen thrusters; MarCO CubeSat cold-gas system

prop26.name: NTR-1 'NERVA' Nuclear Thermal Rocket
prop26.summary: Fission-heated hydrogen engine, Isp ~875 s; shadow-shield rules.
prop26.in_game: Heats liquid hydrogen in a fission reactor: 330 kN vac, Isp ~875 s. LH2 only (tank02 + cryocooler strongly advised). 9 t. Crew must sit in the shield's shadow cone. Needs 30 min of cooldown flow after each burn (~3% extra LH2). Cannot be started below 150 km on inhabited worlds. 10 restarts.

tank11.name: T-TOR Toroidal Tanks
tank11.summary: Ring tank that wraps an engine bell to shorten landers.
tank11.in_game: Ring tank that wraps around an engine bell, making landers and upper stages shorter. Fill set in builder: hypergolic, methalox (dual compartments) or monoprop. M: 2.2 m3 (~2.6 t hypergolic); L: 7.7 m3 (~9 t). Central hole 1.1 / 1.6 m. Dry ~8%.
tank11.real_life: Toroidal propellant tank concepts for compact landers and upper stages

tank12.name: T-ADP Tank Adapters
tank12.summary: Conical adapters that also hold kerolox or methalox.
tank12.in_game: Conical adapters that hold propellant instead of being dead weight (same lengths as stage03). Kerolox or methalox fill set in the builder. S-M 3.6 m3, M-L 14.5 m3, L-XL 36 m3. Dry ~9%.
tank12.real_life: Tapered R-7 / Soyuz strap-on booster tanks

tank13.name: T-LEN Tank Length & Diameter Series
tank13.size_text: XS / S / M / L / XL / XXL
tank13.summary: Extra lengths plus XS and XXL diameters for kerolox/methalox tanks.
tank13.in_game: KSP-style length steps and missing diameters for kerolox / methalox (fill set in builder): XS short and long, S/M half and double, L/XL half, and XXL 7.5 m (super-heavy class). Mass, volume and boil-off scale with the base tank00/tank01 rules.
tank13.real_life: Rocket Lab Electron (XS/S); SpaceX Super Heavy (XXL)

stage12.name: CP-1 Multi-Engine Couplers & Thrust Structure
stage12.summary: Bi/tri/quad couplers and a nine-engine thrust plate with crossfeed.
stage12.in_game: Lets one stack feed several engines or smaller stacks: bi (S->2 XS, M->2 S), tri and quad (L->3/4 S) and a nine-engine L plate (centre + ring of 8, M-class engines). Plumbed (propellant crossfeed) and carries thrust. Extra bottom nodes are node_bottom_N. Mass ~1.5% of the thrust carried.
stage12.real_life: Falcon 9 Octaweb; Titan II twin-engine thrust frame

stage13.name: NC-1 Nose Cones
stage13.summary: Ogive, conical and blunt nose cones for boosters and stacks.
stage13.in_game: Closes the top of a booster or side stack and cuts drag. Ogive (lowest drag, L/D 2), conical (cheap, L/D 1.5) and blunt aero-cap (short, handles heating; L/D 0.5). Mass ~10 kg/m2 of surface. Not a fairing: nothing fits inside.
stage13.real_life: Sounding-rocket and strap-on booster nose cones (Black Brant; Shuttle SRB nose cap)

stage14.name: PS-1 Clamp-Band Payload Separator
stage14.summary: Low-shock clamp band and spring payload separation.
stage14.in_game: Light, low-shock satellite separation: the clamp band releases and springs push the payload away at 0.3-1 m/s with minimal tip-off (no pyro shock, no debris ring). Both halves stay on their own side. Mass 5 / 15 / 40 kg. Cannot re-attach.
stage14.real_life: Marman clamp band; Rocket Lab / Planetary Systems Lightband

stage15.name: AB-1 Landing Airbags
stage15.summary: Inflating airbag cluster for bounce landings.
stage15.in_game: Bounce-landing for probes and small landers: gas generators inflate the lobes in 1 s; survives 25 m/s impacts and bounces to rest, then deflates and retracts. Single use. S: 5.2 m cluster for <1 t landers; M: 9 m for <4 t. Mass 0.12 / 0.45 t. Needs a braking stage or chute first.
stage15.real_life: Mars Pathfinder / Spirit & Opportunity airbags; Boeing Starliner landing airbags

stage16.name: HS-D 'ADEPT' Deployable Heat Shield
stage16.summary: Umbrella-style carbon-fabric heat shield that opens before entry.
stage16.in_game: Umbrella aeroshell: carbon-fabric skin on ribs opens before entry, giving a big low-density shield that fits a narrow fairing. S: 0.625 m stowed -> 2 m; M: 1.25 m stowed -> 6 m. Rated to Mars/Venus entry; gentler than HIAD, single use. Mass 0.03 / 0.35 t.
stage16.real_life: NASA ADEPT (Adaptable Deployable Entry and Placement Technology, SR-1 flight 2018)

stage17.name: PC-R Radial Recovery Chute Pack
stage17.summary: Side-mounted drogue and main chutes to recover spent stages.
stage17.in_game: Radial drogue + main chute pair for recovering spent boosters and stages into the sea (or for radial chute clusters on big capsules). S: brings 5 t to 10 m/s; M: 20 t to 12 m/s on Earth. Stage recovery refunds part cost. Mars: not enough air (see stage09).
stage17.real_life: Space Shuttle SRB recovery parachutes; Rocket Lab Electron booster recovery chute

aero00.name: FS-2 Mk2 Lens Fuselage Sections
aero00.summary: Mk2 lens-profile fuselage (tanks, cabin, bay) matching cockpit02.
aero00.in_game: Body tubes that match the cockpit02 rear face. Tank variants (methalox or kerolox fill; 2.5 / 5 / 10 m3 for 1.25 / 2.5 / 5 m), structural, crew cabin (4 seats, side hatch, 2 Small slots) and service bay (4 Small unpressurised slots). Lifting body: adds some lift. Belly tiles included.
aero00.real_life: Space Shuttle orbiter mid-fuselage; Dream Chaser / X-37B

aero01.name: FA-2 Mk2 Adapters & Tail
aero01.summary: Mk2 to round adapters, bicoupler and twin-pod aft fuselage.
aero01.in_game: Joins Mk2 to round stacks: Mk2 -> M (2.5 m round), Mk2 -> S, Mk2 bicoupler (2 x S bottoms) and an aft fuselage with twin OMS-style pods (two S engine mounts node_bottom_1/2 for prop07/prop13 plus RCS bays). Tank-adapter fill optional.
aero01.real_life: Space Shuttle aft fuselage and OMS pods

aero02.name: FS-3 Mk3 Fuselage Sections (3.75 m)
aero02.summary: 3.75 m Mk3 fuselage barrels: tanks, cabin, structure, service bay.
aero02.in_game: Heavy spaceplane and airliner bodies; front mates cockpit03 and L stacks. Tank variants (methalox / kerolox / LH2 fill; 25 / 50 / 100 m3 for 2.5 / 5 / 10 m), structural, passenger/crew cabin (12 seats, 2 hatches, 4 Small + 1 Rack slots) and service bay (8 Small).
aero02.real_life: Boeing 747 / C-5 fuselage barrels; Space Shuttle orbiter

aero03.name: CB-1 Cargo Bays (Mk2 / Mk3)
aero03.summary: Mk2/Mk3 bays with opening doors (and a rear ramp version).
aero03.in_game: Fuselage with opening doors; payloads on node_payload are shielded like a fairing but can be retrieved and landed again. Door insides are 3 / 10 kW radiators when open. Mk3 ramp variant lowers a rear ramp so M rovers drive in and out. Inner width Mk2 2.1 m, Mk3 3.3 m.
aero03.real_life: Space Shuttle payload bay and door radiators; C-5 / A400M rear ramp

aero04.name: SK-1 Strakes & LERX
aero04.summary: Fuselage strakes that raise the stall angle of attack.
aero04.in_game: Radial lifting blades along the fuselage: create vortices that keep wings lifting at high angle of attack (+30% max AoA before stall), help belly-first re-entry stability. Length 1.5 / 3 / 5 m. 25 kg/m2.
aero04.real_life: F/A-18 leading-edge extensions; Space Shuttle wing glove

aero05.name: VT-1 Tail Fins
aero05.summary: Fixed vertical, twin canted and V-tail fins (rudder node).
aero05.in_game: Fixed vertical stabilisers for yaw stability: single vertical, twin canted (20 deg) or V-tail (45 deg) variants. Trailing-edge node_side_1 takes a jet09 rudder. Height 1.5 / 3 / 5 m. 25 kg/m2.
aero05.real_life: Space Shuttle vertical stabiliser; F-22 twin canted tails

aero06.name: FN-1 Rocket Stabiliser Fins
aero06.summary: Fixed base fins for passive rocket stability.
aero06.in_game: Passive fins at the base of a rocket move the centre of pressure aft for stable ascent without gimbal (sounding rockets, early career). Add drag and burn off on re-entry unless jettisoned with the stage. Span 0.3 / 0.6 / 1.2 m.
aero06.real_life: Saturn V S-IC fins; Black Brant sounding-rocket fins

aero07.name: AB-2 Airbrake
aero07.summary: Hinged speed brake for approach and transonic stability.
aero07.in_game: Deploys to 60 deg on a key press for drag on approach or to stabilise a spaceplane in the transonic regime; auto-retracts above its heat limit (~Mach 3). Drag area 0.5 / 1.8 m2. Mass 20 / 60 kg.
aero07.real_life: F-15 dorsal speed brake; Space Shuttle split-rudder speed brake

jet12.name: CC-1 'SABRE' Precooled Combined-Cycle Engine
jet12.summary: Experimental precooled air-breather that switches to rocket mode.
jet12.in_game: Experimental. Air-breathing up to Mach 5.4 (~600 kN, Isp ~3,500 s using LH2 + intake air), then closes the intake and becomes a hydrolox rocket (~800 kN vac, Isp ~450 s). Integrated spike intake. Heavy (3.5 t); precooler frost/overheat events. For SSTO spaceplanes with Mk3 bodies.
jet12.real_life: Reaction Engines SABRE (ground-tested precooler; never flown)

struct00.name: GD-1 Box Girders
struct00.summary: Light lattice box girders to space parts apart.
struct00.in_game: Light structural spars to space things apart (reactors from crew, antennas from hulls, landing legs outriggers). Surface-attach anywhere along the length; carries power/data lines. 0.3 m section: 8 kg/m; 0.6 m: 25 kg/m.
struct00.real_life: Aluminium space-frame truss girders; Mir Sofora girder

struct01.name: LT-1 Lattice Trusses (S / M)
struct01.in_game: Smaller trusses than station07 for probes, tugs and small stations. Triangular 1.25 m (2 / 4 m) and octagonal 2.5 m (2.5 / 5 m, one unpressurised Medium service bay per 5 m). Routes power, data and coolant. 30 / 80 kg/m.
struct01.real_life: ISS Z1 truss; Northrop Grumman Astromast-style trusses

struct02.name: SR-1 Structural Strut
struct02.summary: Two-ended stiffening strut drawn between any two parts.
struct02.in_game: Two-ended connector drawn between any two parts in the builder (0.3-6 m) to stiffen wobbly stacks and side boosters; breaks at 50 kN. No fluid or power transfer. Ends are node_attach and node_attach_2. 2 kg + 1 kg/m.
struct02.real_life: Space Shuttle External Tank / SRB attach struts

struct03.name: LD-1 Ladders & Handrails
struct03.summary: Fixed/telescoping ladders, EVA handrails and a foot restraint.
struct03.in_game: Crew mobility: fixed ladders (1 / 2 m), a telescoping ladder (1.2 m stowed -> 4 m) for landers, EVA handrails (1 / 2 m) for stations and a portable foot restraint. On EVA in gravity, crew can only climb where ladders exist; in zero-g, handrails set the EVA routes. 3 kg/m.
struct03.real_life: Apollo LM ladder; ISS EVA handrails

struct04.name: HP-1 Radial Pylon / Hardpoint
struct04.summary: Standoff pylon with fuel/power pass-through for side-mounting.
struct04.in_game: Standoff for hanging tanks, engines, nacelles or wings off a hull; the outer node_outboard carries fuel crossfeed, power and data. Standoff 0.6 / 1.2 m, rated 5 / 40 t. Mass 15 / 60 kg.
struct04.real_life: ISS ExPRESS Logistics Carrier FRAM; Shuttle SRB forward attach fitting

station14.name: DP-XS Probe-and-Drogue Docking Port
station14.summary: Small uncrewed docking port that transfers propellant and power.
station14.in_game: Uncrewed docking for probes, tugs and tankers (0.625 m): soft capture, then retract and hard-latch. No crew tunnel, but transfers propellant and power (tanker refuelling). Active/passive halves (like Progress to the station).
station14.real_life: Soyuz / Progress SSVP probe-and-drogue; Apollo probe and drogue

station15.name: GF-1 Grapple Fixture
station15.summary: Fixture that the robotic arm can grab (power/data variant).
station15.in_game: Lets station08 (and rover/robo arms) grab a part. FRGF variant: grab only. PDGF variant: passes power and data, and the arm can 'walk' along modules fitted with them. Needed for CBM berthing. Mass 10 / 25 kg.
station15.real_life: Canadarm2 Power and Data Grapple Fixture; Flight Releasable Grapple Fixture

station16.name: CL-1 Capture Claw
station16.summary: Four-finger claw to capture debris, stages and asteroids.
station16.in_game: Captures objects with no docking port: debris, spent stages, asteroids <20 / 200 t. Fingers close in 5 s and form a rigid structural joint (no crew, fuel or power transfer). Best-in-class for salvage and tug missions. 0.2 / 1.5 kW while moving. Mass 0.15 / 0.8 t.
station16.real_life: ESA ClearSpace-1; Northrop Grumman Mission Extension Vehicle

robo00.name: HG-1 Powered Hinge
robo00.in_game: Single-axis joint (0-180 deg) about the local X axis, with lock. Torque 50 / 500 / 5,000 Nm, 10 deg/s. Builds folding wings, deploying booms, landing-leg mechanisms and ramps. Passes power/data. Moving half is sub-mesh half_b. Mass 3 / 15 / 80 kg.

robo01.name: RT-1 Rotor / Rotation Servo
robo01.summary: Rotation servo or continuous rotor with slip ring.
robo01.in_game: Rotation about the stack axis: servo mode (angle-limited, holds position) or continuous rotor mode up to 60 rpm (fans, spin tables, sun-tracking). Slip ring passes power/data. Torque 20 / 400 / 4,000 Nm. Moving half is half_b. Mass 3 / 20 / 90 kg.
robo01.real_life: Solar Array Drive Assembly; ISS Beta Gimbal Assembly

robo02.name: PS-2 Linear Piston
robo02.summary: Linear actuator along the stack axis, lockable at any length.
robo02.in_game: Linear actuator along the stack axis: extends from 0.4 / 0.8 / 1.6 m to 1.0 / 2.0 / 4.0 m, force 1 / 10 / 100 kN, locks at any length. Levelling legs, lifting cabs, extending docking tunnels. Top half (rod) moves. Mass 5 / 25 / 120 kg.
robo02.real_life: Ball-screw linear actuators (e.g. NASA ATHLETE leg actuators)

robo03.name: TB-1 Deployable Boom
robo03.summary: Canister that deploys a 10 m or 30 m lattice boom.
robo03.in_game: Long standoff from a small package: XS coilable mast 0.6 m -> 10 m; S articulated mast 1.5 m -> 30 m. Separates reactors from crews, radiators and antennas from hulls, and gives gravity-gradient stabilisation. node_top is at the tip in both poses. Mass 8 / 60 kg.
robo03.real_life: SRTM ADAM mast; NuSTAR deployable mast

sci00.name: SC-ENV Environment Sensor Suite
sci00.summary: Small-slot weather, dust and radiation logger (needs aperture).
sci00.in_game: Small slot item. Logs temperature, pressure, wind, dust and radiation continuously (the radiation reading also tracks crew dose). Needs a slot with an aperture (probe bus, service bay, sci03 bay, rover core/cab, hab). 15 W. Mass 12 kg. Science per biome/altitude band, trickled while the vessel is there.

sci01.name: SC-SPC Spectrometer Pack
sci01.summary: Point spectrometer or X-ray diffraction mini-lab in a slot.
sci01.in_game: Small variant: point spectrometer read through an arm contact head or an aperture window. Medium variant: X-ray diffraction mini-lab that takes drill/scoop samples through its top funnel port. Mineralogy science and ISRU ore grading. 25 / 60 W. Mass 15 / 40 kg.

sci02.name: SC-SEI Seismometer Package
sci02.summary: Slot-stowed seismometer placed on the ground by arm or crew.
sci02.in_game: Medium slot item that an arm or crew places on the ground (deployed pose), tethered to the lander. Records quakes and impacts over months; also sounds the interior. Needs quiet: no rover driving within 50 m. 10 W. Mass 30 kg.
sci02.real_life: InSight SEIS; Apollo Passive Seismic Experiment

sci03.name: SB-1 Science Instrument Bay
sci03.summary: SIM-bay stack module with aperture slots and a door.
sci03.in_game: Stack module that turns science into internal equipment: S has 4 Small aperture slots, M 8 Small (or 2 Medium). Door opens (or jettisons) to give instruments a view; closed it protects them on launch and entry. Heaters 20 / 40 W.

sci04.name: SC-RK Experiment Rack
sci04.in_game: Rack slot item (pressurised only: habs, labs, cmd08, rover24-L). Crew-tended biology, materials and microgravity experiments: produces science per crew-hour, best in low or no gravity. 2 kW, 2 kW heat. Mass 0.7 t.

sci05.name: TM-1 Survey Telescope Module
sci05.summary: Stack module with integrated optics for mapping and astronomy.
sci05.in_game: Integrated optics stack module: orbital high-resolution mapping (finds ISRU sites, landing zones and anomalies) and astronomy. Aperture 0.5 / 1.3 m. Needs fine pointing (two power14 wheels) and shade from the Sun. 60 / 300 W. Mass 0.3 / 2.5 t.

sci06.name: SC-SRC Sample Cache
sci06.summary: Sealed sample tubes plus a hand-off container for sample return.
sci06.in_game: Small slot item holding 20 sealed sample tubes from drills and scoops. The orbiting-sample variant is a hand-off container that moves between vessels (rover -> MAV -> orbiter). Samples returned to Earth are worth 3x their field science. 10 W. Mass 18 kg.
sci06.real_life: Perseverance Sample Caching System; Mars Sample Return orbiting sample container

power14.name: RW-1 Reaction Wheel Units
power14.summary: Slot-only reaction wheels in three sizes; saturate, need desat.
power14.in_game: Slot-only attitude control (no bolted-on wheels): torque 5 / 40 / 200 Nm, momentum 50 / 600 / 4,000 Nms, 20 / 60 / 200 W. Saturates under constant torque; desaturates with RCS or automatically via magnetorquers in planetary magnetic fields. Small half-height / Small / Medium slot. Mass 8 / 25 / 110 kg.
power14.real_life: Honeywell HR-series / Hubble reaction wheel assemblies

power15.name: CMG-1 Control Moment Gyro
power15.summary: Rack-size gyro for 3-axis control of very large stations.
power15.in_game: Rack slot (pressurised) or truss service bay item for big stations and ships: 250 Nm, 4,800 Nms, far above reaction wheels for the power (0.1 kW). Four give full 3-axis control of 400 t+ stations without propellant. Mass 0.3 t. Gyroscopic side-effects on spun rings modelled.

power16.name: COM-3 Unfurlable Mesh Relay Antenna
power16.summary: 5 m or 12 m unfurling mesh dish for relay links.
power16.in_game: Relay satellites and deep-space motherships: 5 m (L) or 12 m (XL) dish opens in orbit. Relays other vessels' links (probes and rovers behind a planet). Range to the outer planets at high bandwidth. 0.4 / 1 kW. Must be stowed before burns >0.1 g. Mass 0.15 / 0.45 t.
power16.real_life: NASA TDRS single-access antennas; SMAP 6 m mesh reflector

power17.name: COM-4 Optical Comms Terminal
power17.summary: Laser comms: very high data rate, needs clear skies and stability.
power17.in_game: Laser link with 10-100x the data rate of a radio dish of the same mass, but needs a ground station with clear weather (random cloud outages) and very stable pointing (no burns, no spinning). 22 cm aperture, 60 W. Mass 30 kg.
